title: A For Rent Sign in New Brunswick and Dressings No One Could Inspect
conflicts: 'Sterile': company pages call the 1886-87 products sterile, but the 1888 manual describes antiseptic gauzes, and the International Directory of Company Histories dates dry-heat sterilisation to 1890 while the company timeline dates industrial steam sterilisation to 1891; the story calls the first dressings antiseptic and dates heat sterilisation 1890-91. Founding: company historian says James and Edward started in early 1886 and Robert joined in September 1886; other sources say the three founded it in 1886; Grace's Guide and a newspaper item say 1885 (when they left Seabury & Johnson). Lister: company says Robert heard him in 1876; pharmaphorum says 1885 (not cited); attributed to the company's account. Kilmer joined 1888 (International Directory) or 1889 (company timeline); no year given. 85,000 manual copies is the company's own figure, attributed.
notes: This is the one edition in my group that mentions talQen (in the reflection, on invisible quality made visible by routine checks and records). The repeat screen flagged Jeremy Johnson's Andela edition as same-founder on the shared surname but let it through. Sources are mostly company archive pages, balanced by the 1888 manual itself (Internet Archive) and the International Directory of Company Histories (encyclopedia.com); Britannica and an American Surgeon article were blocked for the verifier.
